title: Victoria votes today, with Labor tipped to lose
lede: Victorians are choosing a government today after twelve years of Labor, and polls point to a Coalition win under Jess Wilson. Wall Street also finished its best week in more than a year.

stories.headline: Victoria votes as Labor faces a heavy defeat
stories.summary: Election day has arrived in Victoria, with about half of the state's 4.7 million voters already having voted early or by post. The final Newspoll (20-25 November) had the Coalition on 33% of the primary vote, Labor 20%, One Nation 18% and the Greens 17%, with the Coalition ahead 57.5 to 42.5 after preferences. Labor, now led by Ben Carroll after Jacinta Allan resigned in July, has been hurt by Big Build corruption allegations and state debt. Liberal leader Jess Wilson may form government with a historically low primary vote, and One Nation is expected to win more than 20%. ABC election coverage starts at 6pm AEDT.
stories.why: A big swing against Labor in Victoria is a warning sign about cost-of-living anger that federal Labor will also face.

stories.headline: RBA tipped to hold at 4.85% as recession fears grow
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank has raised the cash rate by 125 basis points this year to 4.85%. After October inflation jumped to 4.9% (trimmed mean 3.8%), a hold at the 7-8 December meeting is still the most likely outcome, though further hikes cannot be ruled out. Governor Michele Bullock has warned the economy will feel like a recession, and a Guardian report says mortgage holders' confidence is at its lowest since 1994. Treasurer Jim Chalmers has flagged that his mid-year budget update will forecast slower growth and higher unemployment, and the AFR says economists are pointing him to spending cuts.
stories.why: Mortgage and rent pressure is not easing yet, and a weaker jobs market hits young graduates first.

stories.headline: Wall Street posts its best week in over a year as Anthropic and Nvidia swing
stories.summary: The S&P 500 rose 1.6% on Friday to 7,297 and gained 5.6% for the week, its strongest since April 2025. The Dow added 1.2% and the Nasdaq 2.3%. Anthropic, which raised a record US$93.5 billion in its IPO last week, rose 11% to US$91.88, above its US$83 issue price after dipping below it on Tuesday. Nvidia rattled markets after CEO Jensen Huang resigned and was then reinstated, with CNBC reporting the shares jumped more than 30% on the day he returned. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.94%.
stories.why: If your super is in index funds, you own a lot of these AI stocks, so their swings flow into your balance.

stories.headline: Schools push back on Google's AI search summaries
stories.summary: Los Angeles school officials have quietly disabled Google's AI Overview summaries on school-issued devices. Google says search and AI are deeply integrated and told The New York Times that if schools ban AI, students will not have access to search. New York and Los Angeles announced one-year moratoriums on student use of generative AI in September, and hundreds of Google employees have signed a petition asking for a way to turn AI features off without losing search.
stories.why: It is an early test of whether AI can be switched off inside everyday tools you rely on for study and work.

stories.headline: New drug roughly doubles survival in advanced pancreatic cancer
stories.summary: The US FDA has approved daraxonrasib for metastatic pancreatic cancer in patients whose disease has progressed on at least one earlier treatment. In the trial, median overall survival was 13.2 months versus 6.7 months on chemotherapy, and the European Commission has also approved it. It is not a cure, but it is the first of a new class of targeted RAS-blocking drugs for one of the deadliest cancers.
stories.why: A real step forward for a cancer with few options, and a sign of how fast targeted drugs are moving from trial to patients.

stories.headline: Trump urges Russia and Ukraine not to expand the war as the Iran conflict drags on
stories.summary: After meeting NATO chief Mark Rutte at Mar-a-Lago, Donald Trump urged both Russia and Ukraine to avoid actions that expand the war; his wording added Ukraine to a statement NATO framed around Russia. Last month he waived sanctions on a Russian diesel deal aimed at lowering fuel prices, which drew criticism from European leaders and Republicans. Ukraine's president Volodymyr Zelensky has publicly criticised Trump's warm stance toward Vladimir Putin. Meanwhile the US war with Iran continues; Brent crude has swung between US$72 and US$114 since February and closed Friday at US$90.84.
stories.why: The war keeps oil high, which keeps petrol and shipping costs, and inflation, high.

watch: Victoria's election count tonight, then the RBA decision on 7-8 December, which markets expect to be a hold.

title: Australian inflation jumps to 4.9% as jobs weaken
lede: Prices rose 4.9% in the year to October while unemployment sits at its highest since 2021, squeezing the RBA and the Treasurer. Meanwhile Wall Street is rebounding from a brutal AI-led sell-off.

stories.headline: Australian inflation jumps to 4.9%, led by fuel and electricity
stories.summary: The ABS says consumer prices rose 4.9% in the year to October, up from 4.3% and well above the RBA's 2-3% target. Fuel was up about 33% over the year and electricity 25% as government rebates ended. The RBA's preferred trimmed mean measure rose to 3.8% from 3.6%, and building costs rose 5.1%. Treasurer Jim Chalmers called it "a very serious moment". Economists at KPMG and NAB expect the RBA to hold at its 7-8 December meeting, with NAB still expecting cuts from August; the IMF urged the RBA to stay ready to tighten if prices worsen. The IMF also expects growth to slow to 1.9% in 2026 and 1.6% in 2027.
stories.why: Rent, mortgage and petrol pressure is not easing yet, but most economists see this as a peak rather than the start of another rate hike.

stories.headline: Unemployment at 4.9%, the highest since 2021
stories.summary: Australia's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rose to 4.9% in October, the highest since October 2021, ABS data show. Employment fell by 44,000 and unemployment rose by 18,000, while hours worked fell 0.2%. Chalmers has warned unemployment will pass 5% and is due to deliver the mid-year budget update in about three weeks, promising substantial savings. Analysts say the Treasurer must trim spending without tipping a weakening economy into recession.
stories.why: Falling inflation relief plus a softer jobs market makes entry-level and graduate hiring harder, and raises the odds of rate cuts next year.

stories.headline: Wall Street rebounds after an AI-led sell-off
stories.summary: The S&P 500 fell 8.6% in the week to 20 November, led by AI stocks, then gained 3.9% through Wednesday, on track for its best Thanksgiving week since 2008 if Friday's half-day session holds. US markets were shut Thursday and US futures point sharply higher. The VIX fear gauge peaked near 36 on 20 November and was still about 26 on Tuesday. Nvidia has reportedly halted chip shipments to south-east Asia, and the Bank of England warned of growing financial risks from opaque AI borrowing.
stories.why: Index funds and super funds hold heavy AI exposure, so this volatility reaches ordinary portfolios.

stories.headline: SAP reportedly weighs cutting at least 10,000 jobs in AI overhaul
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter, that German software maker SAP is preparing a plan to cut at least 10,000 positions as it reshapes its business for the AI era, following reductions at Oracle and Microsoft. The plan has not been confirmed by the company.
stories.why: Software and tech roles are the front line of AI-driven restructuring, which matters for anyone building a career in tech.

stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine trade heavy strikes as oil climbs
stories.summary: Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv and other regions from late Wednesday into Thursday, killing at least 10 and wounding 58, Ukrainian authorities said, while Ukraine hit Russian oil facilities. President Trump says he urged Vladimir Putin to pull back and calls a peace deal a strong possibility, but recent US-mediated talks produced only a prisoner swap agreement. Zelensky says Russia is preparing another major strike on the power grid. Separately, Brent crude rose about 1.3% to US$92.82 after Yemen's Houthis reportedly struck a Saudi refinery, with the US-Israeli war with Iran ongoing.
stories.why: Oil is a key driver of Australian fuel prices, which are up about a third in a year.

stories.headline: Alzheimer's drug diranersen slows decline 38% in phase 2 extension; FDA clears Neuralink pivotal trial
stories.summary: In the long-term extension of the phase 2 CELIA trial, Biogen's diranersen (BIIB080), a twice-yearly injection, slowed clinical decline by 38% on the CDR-SB scale at 96 weeks at the 60 mg dose, up from 26% at 76 weeks. Patients still declined, only more slowly, and larger trials are needed. Separately, the FDA approved Neuralink's pivotal study, the first US pivotal trial of an implantable brain-computer interface.
stories.why: Early-stage results, but a sign that Alzheimer's treatment is broadening beyond current drugs, and brain implants are moving toward real trials.

stories.headline: Albanese at the halfway mark as Victoria heads to the polls
stories.summary: Commentators say Prime Minister Anthony Albanese reaches the midpoint of his term with a big hill to climb, with the economy the main test. Victorians vote tomorrow, with Crikey reporting that Jess Wilson's Coalition is set to end 12 years of Labor government.
stories.why: A Labor loss in Victoria and a weak economy raise the political stakes ahead of the mid-year budget update.

watch: The Victorian state election tomorrow, then the RBA board meeting on 7-8 December.

stories.why: Real episodes start with the next morning run.
